topic_and_scope: A narrative analysis of recurrence patterns of interstitial lung disease after lung transplantation, with emphasis on disease subtypes, genetic factors (notably telomere biology), immune interactions, and implications for post-transplant management and prevention strategies.
main_themes: Disease-specific recurrence patterns after lung transplantation across ILD subtypes
Genetic and telomere biology influences on post-transplant outcomes and recurrence risk
Post-transplant management, surveillance, and immunosuppression strategies to prevent recurrence
main_findings: Recurrence of ILD after lung transplantation varies by ILD subtype, with DIP being frequently reported; timing can be early (as soon as one month) and recurrence patterns are influenced by host factors, antigen exposure, and immune events.

Telomere length abnormalities and telomere-related mutations are associated with adverse post-transplant outcomes (e.g., bone marrow dysfunction, PGD, CLAD) and potential recurrence risk, but findings are inconsistent due to variations in defining short telomeres across studies.

key_gaps.description: Standardized definition and measurement of short telomere length (ST) and harmonized cutoff values across studies to enable consistent risk stratification and outcome interpretation.
Need for prospective, multicenter data collection and consensus protocols (registries) to define, detect, and manage ILD recurrence after lung transplantation.

future_directions.title: Standardize telomere-length assessment and integrate into candidate selection and post-transplant care
future_directions.rationale: Develop a shared protocol for measuring telomere length (e.g., standardized assay with clearly defined percentile cutoffs) across centers. Prospectively evaluate how ST length and telomere-related mutations influence donor-recipient interactions, bone marrow reserve, infection risk, and graft function. Use findings to tailor immunosuppression (e.g., avoiding intensive T-cell depletion in ST patients) and monitor for hematologic or extrapulmonary dysfunction, potentially reducing recurrence and retransplantation needs.

future_directions.title: Establish a multicenter international registry for post-LTx ILD recurrence with standardized definitions
future_directions.rationale: Create a centralized, prospective database capturing ILD subtype, recurrence timing, histology, donor/recipient factors, telomere/genetic data, immunosuppression regimens, infections, and retransplantation outcomes. Enable large-scale analyses, validation of risk factors, and development of evidence-based surveillance and management guidelines. Include tissue banking and biospecimen collections to enable mechanistic studies.

future_directions.title: Develop risk-stratified post-transplant surveillance protocols for early recurrence detection
future_directions.rationale: Use ILD subtype, telomere status, and immune factors to tailor surveillance (imaging frequency, biomarkers, and selective biopsies). Test these protocols in prospective cohorts to determine sensitivity, specificity, cost-effectiveness, and impact on graft survival and patient quality of life. Establish clear thresholds for diagnostic interventions and treatment initiation upon signs of recurrence.

future_directions.title: Investigate immunosuppression optimization to reduce recurrence and improve graft outcomes
future_directions.rationale: Conduct comparative studies to delineate the role of mTOR inhibitors (sirolimus, everolimus) vs calcineurin inhibitors in reducing recurrence risk for high-burden ILDs (e.g., IPF-related ILD, sarcoidosis, PLCH) while balancing adverse events such as bronchial dehiscence. Explore personalization of regimens based on telomere status, bone marrow reserve, and infectious risk. Include randomized or well-designed prospective observational studies within the registry framework.

future_directions.title: Elucidate mechanisms of donor–recipient immune interactions and autoantibody-driven recurrence
future_directions.rationale: Investigate the contribution of tissue-specific autoantibodies, recipient-derived granulomas, and antigen exposure (including acute rejection episodes) to recurrence. Identify biomarkers (autoantibodies, immune cell profiles, cytokine signatures) that predict recurrence risk. Use mechanistic insight to inform targeted immunomodulatory strategies or tolerogenic approaches to prevent recurrence without compromising overall graft immunity.

future_directions.title: Develop disease-specific recurrence prevention strategies and trials
future_directions.rationale: Design targeted approaches for diseases with notable recurrence (e.g., PLCH, LAM, PAP, CTD-ILD) including lifestyle interventions (smoking cessation for PLCH), optimization of disease-specific therapies around the transplant period (e.g., continued mTOR inhibition in LAM when appropriate), and exploring adjunctive treatments (e.g., bone marrow–targeted therapies for PAP) in carefully selected patients. Pilot studies or small multicenter trials should assess feasibility, safety, and signals of efficacy on recurrence rates.

future_directions.title: Investigate donor-telomere length considerations in donor selection and graft outcomes
future_directions.rationale: Assess whether donor telomere length influences post-transplant graft function, recipient immune responses, or recurrence risk. If associations are found, evaluate donor selection policies or preconditioning strategies that consider telomere biology to optimize long-term graft survival and minimize recurrence across ILD subtypes.

future_directions.title: Clarify retransplantation outcomes and develop decision frameworks for recurrent ILD
future_directions.rationale: Collect data on retransplantation in recipients with prior ILD recurrence to identify which patients derive meaningful survival and quality-of-life benefits. Develop evidence-based criteria (e.g., timing, disease activity, extrapulmonary involvement) to guide retransplantation decisions and optimize patient selection.

future_directions.title: Advance noninvasive diagnostics to distinguish recurrence from infection, rejection, and other allograft dysfunction
future_directions.rationale: Validate tools such as donor-derived cell-free DNA, advanced imaging biomarkers, and BAL or serum biomarkers to differentiate ILD recurrence from infection or rejection. This will enable earlier, targeted treatment and reduce unnecessary invasive procedures, ultimately improving surveillance efficiency and patient outcomes.
